content:
maria: Heads-up — customer-reporting: tenant A's dashboard showed 3 rows from tenant B after I used quick-switch and toggled filters. reproducible 2x.
kevin: ugh. any stack traces / logs? sounds like a scope/caching issue.
sam: did we recently change prefetch for console panels? iirc that touched the route-affinity layer.
maria: yeah might be prefetch. saw this in the console access logs: `GET /api/panels?prefetch=true` came with `x-tenant-id: tenant-a` but the subsequent prefetch worker call to `/internal/panel-data` had `x-tenant-id: ` missing.
emily: missing header is suspicious — fallback code in router adds header from session cookie, but that cookie is `workspaces` and we introduced header normalization last month. could be header name mismatch (`x-tenant-id` vs `x-workspace-id`).
kevin: put a quick grep in prod logs: `grep -R "internal/panel-data" | grep x-workspace-id` shows some hits but also a chunk with no tenant header. infra-bot: flagged 7 requests in the last 10m with null tenant header.
maria: repro steps: 1) open tenant-b dashboard 2) quick-switch to tenant-a via header switcher 3) open panel with prefetch enabled -> observe row bleed.
sam: sounds like affinity fallback logic: when route affinity fails we call shared fallback route which sets `X-Org: shared` and reuses cached response. if affinity routing didn't attach tenant label, cached shared content served.
emily: that aligns with telemetry — panel fetch latency was very low for the leaked rows (cache hit) and trace shows `route-fallback -> cache-read` branch. rollout UX question: our canary config for prefetch routing was 10% to new affinity-aware proxy. maybe those 10% are fine, but the fallback code path still has the old behavior.
kevin: immediate mitigation: disable prefetch for console panels globally (quick toggle in console) or make fallback reject on missing tenant header. which is less risky?
maria: i'd rather reject (401/422) so we fail loudly rather than leak. but customers might see errors.
sam: agree on failing loudly for now; we'll pair with a short incident banner and rollback prefetch if needed.
emily: also need a postmortem item — add a unit / integration test to assert `internal/panel-data` always receives `x-tenant-id` or bails.
kevin: action items: - sam: add middleware that asserts tenant header and returns 422 if absent (short PR) - maria: draft customer banner + notify CS - emily: telemetry alert for cache hits on internal routes without tenant header - infra-bot: create rollout blocker for prefetch canary until header fix is in.
infra-bot: created issue INFRA-8472 and rollout blocker tag applied to canary pipeline.
maria: i'll test the middleware locally against quick-switch flows. can someone point to the exact header normalization change?
emily: PR #4123 changed header mapping from `x-workspace-id` -> `x-tenant-id` and added a fallback mapping step. i suspect the worker uses the old env var `PREFETCH_HEADER` still set to `x-workspace-id`.
sam: good catch — config drift between console front-end and prefetch worker. that explains selective failures.
kevin: ok prioritize config sync and middleware. if we push middleware in next hour, we can flip canary to 0% and monitor.
maria: on it, testing now. i[31m:warning:[0m found a quick repro where missing header happens only on cold worker start (cache warm). bringing more logs.
emily: sounds like worker startup path reads headers differently. add integration test that runs a fresh worker process and hits prefetch sequence.
sam: long term: unify header name in a single constants package and import in front-end, proxy, worker. also add schema validation on internal APIs.
maria: noted. thanks team. will update when middleware PR is up. :thumbsup:
